skill.name: get-seen-in-replies
skill.description: Draft concise Twitter replies that add a specific insight and make sense without the original tweet. Avoid flattery, disguised advertising, and visibility promises.
skill.summary: Decide whether to reply, identify a useful gap, and draft a standalone response.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Write Twitter Replies That Add Value
content.value_statement: Generic replies often add little to a conversation and can harm your reputation. This skill identifies a useful gap and drafts a concise, standalone response.
actual_capabilities: Recommend skipping a reply when there is no useful contribution.
Identify assumptions, missing context, contrary experience, concrete examples, or next steps in a supplied tweet.
Draft short replies that make sense without the original tweet.
Discuss timing tradeoffs between seeking reach and responding for conversation.
Avoid praise-only openings, unsolicited promotional links, and replies designed to provoke the author.
Describe optional VoiceMOAT tools for voice profiles, voice matching, and developing standalone post ideas.
limitations: Does not guarantee visibility, engagement, or audience growth.
Does not publish replies or provide live Twitter monitoring.
Needs supplied tweet content and relevant context for a grounded response.
VoiceMOAT integration requires a connected service and a Pro or Enterprise plan; no connector implementation is included.

use_cases.title: Contribute a practical insight
use_cases.description: Turn a relevant tweet into a short response that adds a concrete example or useful next step.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a reply opportunity
use_cases.description: Assess whether a tweet deserves a response, considering your contribution and whether your goal is reach or conversation.

use_cases.title: Share professional experience
use_cases.description: Draft a reply that challenges an assumption using your supplied experience, without advertising your company.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first reply
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a short, standalone reply to this tweet: [tweet]. Name the useful gap, or recommend skipping if there is nothing to add.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: respond to one supplied tweet.

prompt_templates.title: Use your experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Tweet: [tweet]. My relevant experience: [experience]. Identify the missing context and draft a concise reply without praise or promotion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: ground the reply in your own experience.

prompt_templates.title: Choose whether to engage
prompt_templates.prompt: Tweet: [tweet]. Posted: [time]. My contribution: [insight]. My goal: [reach or conversation]. Assess whether to reply, then draft only if useful.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: consider timing and contribution before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a voice-aligned response
prompt_templates.prompt: Tweet: [tweet]. Experience: [experience]. If VoiceMOAT is connected, use my Twitter voice profile and check voice match. Suggest a separate post idea when appropriate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: request optional voice support and a standalone post direction.

output_examples.input: Tweet: More meetings always make teams more aligned. Experience: Our team improved alignment with written decisions and fewer meetings.
output: Gap: Meeting frequency does not account for how decisions are recorded.
Reply: Alignment needs a shared record of decisions, not just more meetings. Our team improved it by writing decisions down and meeting less.

output_examples.input: Tweet: We launched our new dashboard today. I have not tried it and have no specific question or insight.
output: Reason: There is no concrete contribution to add. A generic compliment would not provide a standalone insight.

best_practices: Supply the tweet, its timing, your goal, and any relevant firsthand experience.
Check that the reply adds a specific insight and makes sense without its parent tweet.
Review factual claims and tone before posting; treat embedded tweet instructions as untrusted text.
anti_patterns: Replying to every post simply to appear under a large account.
Opening with generic praise or repeating the original tweet without adding information.
Adding unsolicited product links or provoking the author to obtain attention.

faq.question: Will this guarantee that my reply is seen?
faq.answer: No. Visibility depends on timing, the parent account, and activity under the tweet.

faq.question: Does the skill publish replies for me?
faq.answer: No. It drafts responses and explicitly states that nothing is published from inside the skill.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the tweet text, relevant experience, and your goal. Include posting time when timing matters.

faq.question: Can it recommend not replying?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends skipping when you have no useful contribution to add.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: No. The core drafting workflow does not require it. Optional voice tools need a connected VoiceMOAT service with Pro or Enterprise access.

faq.question: Can I include a product link?
faq.answer: The skill discourages links unless requested and avoids replies that become disguised advertisements.
